author: Ahmed Ibrahim
title: Annunciation Catholic Church Shooting: What We Know So Far
text:
MINNEAPOLIS, August 28, 2025 – A shooting at a Catholic school in South Minneapolis on Wednesday morning claimed the lives of two young children and injured 17 worshippers during morning Mass.
Tragic attack rocks Minneapolis community during school Mass.
A gunman killed two children and wounded 17 others at a Minneapolis Catholic church.
- Two children, ages 8 and 10, were killed during Mass at Annunciation Catholic Church.
- Seventeen others, including 14 children and three seniors, were injured but expected to survive.
- The shooter, Robin Westman, 23, died by suicide and legally purchased three firearms.
- Authorities are investigating the incident as an act of
domestic terrorismand a hate crime targeting Catholics. - The attack occured just three days into the new school year.
The latest: Minneapolis Police Chief Brian O’Hara confirmed Wednesday afternoon that the 14 children and three senior parishioners who were wounded are expected to recover.
The big picture: The violence, which unfolded just three days after the fall semester began, sent shockwaves across the city, state, and nation. Leaders, including President Trump and Pope Leo XIV, offered their sympathies to the community.
This incident marks one of the most severe acts of gun violence against a Minnesota school in decades.
What happened
O’Hara stated that the assailant approached Annunciation Catholic Church from the side during a service. The gunman then opened fire into the windows, striking the children, ages 8 and 10, who were seated in the pews.
The shooter
Authorities identified the assailant as 23-year-old Robin Westman, who died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound at the back of the church. Westman had no known criminal history and was armed with a rifle, a pistol, and a shotgun. All firearms were recently purchased legally, according to O’Hara.
Reactions to the violence
“This was a deliberate act of violence against innocent children and other people worshiping,” O’Hara said.”The sheer cruelty and cowardice of firing into a church full of children is absolutely incomprehensible.”
Mayor Jacob Frey urged action beyond condolences: “Don’t just say this is about thoughts and prayers right now. These kids were literally praying.”
Law enforcement response
The shooting, reported around 8:30 a.m., prompted a significant law enforcement response. The Bureau of Criminal Apprehension,State Patrol,and FBI joined local agencies at the scene.
Investigation and motive
Authorities are continuing their investigation to determine a motive.O’Hara mentioned that a video, believed to have been posted online by the shooter before being removed, is under review.
FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed the agency is investigating the attack as “an act of domestic terrorism and hate crime targeting Catholics.”
Broader context
The church shooting occurred at the close of a violent 24-hour period in Minneapolis. Police responded to three other fatal shootings between Tuesday evening and early Wednesday morning.
O’Hara clarified that the church attack “does not appear to be related to any other shooting in the city.”
